@graph.name: UK Student Loan Repayment Calculator
@graph.description: Income-contingent UK student loan PAYE calculator using GOV.UK 2026/27 Plan 1, 2, 4, 5 and postgraduate thresholds.

mainEntity.name: Is this the same as a US student loan calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. UK undergraduate and postgraduate loans repay a percentage of income above a plan threshold. The US student loan calculator on this site models a fixed amortising monthly payment. Switching the currency on that page does not produce a UK payslip deduction.

Plan 5 covers England and Wales courses that started on or after 1 August 2023. Plan 2 covers England and Wales 1 September 2012 to 31 July 2023. Plan 1 is earlier England/Wales and most Northern Ireland loans. Plan 4 is Scotland. Postgraduate loans use a separate 6% rate. Confirm on GOV.UK or your Student Finance account.

mainEntity.name: What if I have a postgraduate loan as well?

acceptedAnswer.text: GOV.UK says you repay 6% of income over the postgraduate threshold and 9% of income over the lowest undergraduate plan threshold you have. Tick the postgraduate box on this page to add both.

mainEntity.name: Why might PAYE take a pound less than 9% of the excess?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payroll rounds the deduction down to the nearest pound. This page shows the unrounded pence and the PAYE amount.

mainEntity.name: Does this show when the loan is paid off?

acceptedAnswer.text: It projects it. The payslip deduction uses the published 2026/27 thresholds exactly. The payoff projection is an estimate: it depends on your salary growth, the interest rate you enter, and thresholds staying at today's levels.
